[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an [[:en:Toraijin|immigrant]] clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]], and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title [[:en:Sukune|Sukune]]''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]] clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[:en:Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[:en:Kansai region|Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[:en:List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[:en:Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[:en:Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[:en:Takakuraji|Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname [[:en:Ason|Ason]], and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan [[:en:Yamatonoaya clan|Yamatonoaya clan]], but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami [[:en:Shake (social class)|Shrine family]] in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

（[[公家]]・[[華族]]（[[子爵]]））
[[小森家]]（[[地下家]]）
[[多紀氏]]（[[武家]]）
[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an [[:en:Toraijin|immigrant]] clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]], and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title [[:en:Sukune|Sukune]]''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]] clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] they advanced east through [[:en:Chūgoku region|Chugoku]] region to the [[:en:Kansai region|Kansai region]]. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the [[:en:List of emperors of Japan|Yamato dynasty]] ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ([[:en:Emperor of Japan|emperor]]). The dynasty expanded its power to [[:en:Chūbu region|Chubu]] and [[:en:Kantō region|Kanto]] regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} [[:en:Watatsumi|Watatsumi]]. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[:en:Takakuraji|Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname [[:en:Ason|Ason]], and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan [[:en:Yamatonoaya clan|Yamatonoaya clan]], but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami [[:en:Shake (social class)|Shrine family]] in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

[[ja:丹波氏]][[ko:단바씨]] [[ja:丹波氏]][[ko:단바씨]] [[ja:丹波氏]][[ko:단바씨]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11368583]] Wikidata name: Tanba clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:50, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Distinguish|{{ill|Tsumori clan|ja|津守氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}}} {{Infobox Japanese clan|氏名=丹波氏|image=|氏姓=丹波[[宿禰]] → 丹波[[朝臣]]|始祖=|出自=称[[坂上氏]]|氏祖=称[[阿知使主]]（[[後漢]][[霊帝 (漢)|霊帝]]後裔）|種別=[[諸蕃]]？|本貫=|人物=[[丹波康頼]]
[[丹波時長]]
[[丹波忠守]]|後裔='''[[錦小路家]]'''
（[[公家]]・[[華族]]（[[子爵]]））
[[小森家]]（[[地下家]]）
[[多紀氏]]（[[武家]]）
[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an {{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|WD=Q11561926|lt=immigrant}} clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}}, and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|WD=Q11455653|lt=Sukune}}''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}} clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} they advanced east through {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chugoku}} region to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region}}. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|WD=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|WD=Q134638|lt=Chubu}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|WD=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|WD=Q4807592|lt=Ason}}, and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|en|Yamatonoaya clan|WD=Q10870550|lt=Yamatonoaya clan}}, but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami {{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|WD=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family}} in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

[[丹波時長]]
[[丹波忠守]]|後裔='''[[錦小路家]]'''
（[[公家]]・[[華族]]（[[子爵]]））
[[小森家]]（[[地下家]]）
[[多紀氏]]（[[武家]]）
[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an {{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|WD=Q11561926|lt=immigrant}} clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}}, and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|WD=Q11455653|lt=Sukune}}''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}} clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} they advanced east through {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chugoku}} region to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region}}. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|WD=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|WD=Q134638|lt=Chubu}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|WD=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|WD=Q4807592|lt=Ason}}, and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|en|Yamatonoaya clan|WD=Q10870550|lt=Yamatonoaya clan}}, but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami {{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|WD=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family}} in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an {{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|WD=Q11561926|lt=immigrant}} clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}}, and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|WD=Q11455653|lt=Sukune}}''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}} clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} they advanced east through {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chugoku}} region to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region}}. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|WD=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|WD=Q134638|lt=Chubu}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|WD=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|WD=Q4807592|lt=Ason}}, and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|en|Yamatonoaya clan|WD=Q10870550|lt=Yamatonoaya clan}}, but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami {{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|WD=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family}} in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an {{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|WD=Q11561926|lt=immigrant}} clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}}, and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|WD=Q11455653|lt=Sukune}}''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}} clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} they advanced east through {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chugoku}} region to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region}}. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|WD=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|WD=Q134638|lt=Chubu}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|WD=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|WD=Q4807592|lt=Ason}}, and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|en|Yamatonoaya clan|WD=Q10870550|lt=Yamatonoaya clan}}, but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami {{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|WD=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family}} in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

[[丹波時長]]
[[丹波忠守]]|後裔='''[[錦小路家]]'''
（[[公家]]・[[華族]]（[[子爵]]））
[[小森家]]（[[地下家]]）
[[多紀氏]]（[[武家]]）
[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an {{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|WD=Q11561926|lt=immigrant}} clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}}, and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|WD=Q11455653|lt=Sukune}}''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Nishikinokoji family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}} clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} they advanced east through {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chugoku}} region to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region}}. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|WD=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|WD=Q134638|lt=Chubu}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|WD=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|WD=Q4807592|lt=Ason}}, and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|en|Yamatonoaya clan|WD=Q10870550|lt=Yamatonoaya clan}}, but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata district|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=the Hoga Seyaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami {{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|WD=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family}} in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===

[[丹波時長]]
[[丹波忠守]]|後裔='''[[錦小路家]]'''
（[[公家]]・[[華族]]（[[子爵]]））
[[小森家]]（[[地下家]]）
[[多紀氏]]（[[武家]]）
[[施薬院氏]]（[[地下人]]）}} '''The Tanba clan''' (丹波氏) is a Japanese clan. It is generally considered to be an {{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|WD=Q11561926|lt=immigrant|1=Toraijin}} clan. They claim to be descended from [[:en:Achi no omi|Achi no Omi,]] who immigrated during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin|1=Emperor Ōjin}}, and their original surname is {{ill|10=ja|11=坂上氏|Sakanoue|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Sakanoue clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10928477}} . During the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}}, '''they were given the title {{ill|Sukune|en|Sukune|WD=Q11455653|lt=Sukune|1=Sukune}}''' . The {{ill|10=ja|11=錦小路家|Nishikinokoji family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Q22129074|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q22129074}} was one of the clan's noble {{ill|10=ja|11=堂上家|Tōshōke|lt=families|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tōshōke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11427847}} , and others included {{ill|10=ja|11=金保氏|the Kaneyasu family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (later {{ill|10=ja|11=多紀氏|the Taki family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Taki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16141794}} ) and {{ill|10=ja|11=施薬院氏|the Seyakuin family|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} .{{Clear}} == Genealogy == The Tanba clan split off from the {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe|1=Amabe clan}} clan. The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020}} In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinsen Shōjiroku|qq=}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|qq=}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-hohi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|simple|User: Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja|6=en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanomichine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, together with the descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}} are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}}'' descended from {{ill|Takamagahara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamagahara|qq=}} (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heaven|qq=}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|lt=Owari|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Province|qq=}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba Province|qq=}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|lt=Owari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori|ja|津守氏|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsumori clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|WD=Q65272445|lt=Amabe|1=Amabe clan}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba|ja|丹波氏|1=Tanba clan|2=ja|3=丹波氏|4=ko|5=단바씨|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|en|6=simple|7=User:Immanuelle/Tanba_clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanba clan|qq=}} clans.{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}} The {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|simple|User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson-zoku|qq=}} descended from [[Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|qq=}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|lt=reed beds|reed bed|simple|User:Immanuelle/reed bed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/reed bed|qq=}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Led by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu|1=Emperor Jimmu}} they advanced east through {{ill|Chūgoku region|en|Chūgoku region|WD=Q127864|lt=Chugoku|1=Chūgoku region}} region to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region|1=Kansai region}}. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|WD=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty|1=List of emperors of Japan}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakoku|qq=}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okimi|qq=}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=emperor|1=Emperor of Japan}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|WD=Q134638|lt=Chubu|1=Chūbu region}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|WD=Q132480|lt=Kanto|1=Kantō region}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|qq=}}}} However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohoakari|qq=}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|lt=sea deity|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of water deities|qq=}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi|1=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|en|Takakuraji|WD=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji|1=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}} == Origin == The family name was first established during the reign of {{ill|10=ja|11=丹波康頼|Tanba no Yasuyori|lt=Tanba Yasuyori|de|Tanba no Yasuyori|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Tanba no Yasuyori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1466794}} when he was given the surname Tanba no {{ill|Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukune|qq=}}. Later, they were given the surname {{ill|Ason|en|Ason|WD=Q4807592|lt=Ason|1=Ason}}, and over the generations, they produced many physicians, including doctors of medicine, acupuncture doctors, and {{nihongo|{{ill|Bureau of Pharmacy|ja|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|simple|User:Immanuelle/Bureau_of_Pharmacy|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|13=User:Immanuelle/Bureau of Pharmacy|qq=}}|典薬寮|1=Bureau of Pharmacy|2=ja|3=典薬寮|4=fr|5=Bureau de pharmacie|Ten'yaku-ryō}}.{{Citation needed|date=2020th year 9月}}、Tanba Yasuyori is recognized as a figure from the early 10th century, during the middle Heian period, while Sakagami Naohirokuni is identified as a figure from the early 8th century, during the middle Nara period. The discrepancy of about 200 years between their times makes the origins of the former highly questionable. As mentioned above, the Tanba clan is generally considered to have originated from the Tanba clan, a descendant of the immigrant clan {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|en|Yamatonoaya clan|WD=Q10870550|lt=Yamatonoaya clan|1=Yamatonoaya clan}}, but the family founder Tanba Yasuyori was from {{ill|10=ja|11=天田郡|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|en|Fukuchiyama, Kyoto|lt=Amada County|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Amata District, Kyoto|WD=Q4740432}}, where the Tanba no [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Kuni no Miyatsuko]] (Tanba Cho) lived, and the Daido Ruijuho contains a description of {{ill|10=ja|11=大同類聚方|the Hoga Seyaku|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|1=Q11433347|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11433347}}, which was passed down to the '''Tanba Chojin''' members of the Amaterasu Tamami {{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|WD=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family|1=Shake (social class)}} in Amada County. == Genealogy == === Head of the family ===
